route: The UK has no visa route for non-working people of independent means (the Home Office lists work, study, family, investor/talent routes only; the retired and the independently wealthy cannot settle). A resident on any long-stay visa of over 6 months pays the Immigration Health Surcharge up front, which gives full NHS access.
policy: Immigration Health Surcharge, GBP 1,035 per adult per year, paid for each year of visa; NHS care then free at point of use. Private cover not required.

sources.title: Pay for UK healthcare as part of your immigration application: how much you have to pay
sources.quote: £1,035 per year for all other visa and immigration applications
sources.measures: Annual surcharge per adult applicant, set by regulation; 5-year visa = 5 payments up front.

typical_private.description: Comprehensive private medical insurance incl. outpatient for two 45-year-olds (Bupa, AXA Health, Vitality), about GBP 120 to 150 a month for two. Estimate from a comparison guide and Bupa's published age table (both read via search excerpts; Bupa's page blocks plain fetches); low confidence.

eu_citizen_difference: EU citizens no longer have free movement; after Brexit the same visa and IHS rules apply (except Irish citizens, with no IHS).
spot_check: Matches the IHS rate on gov.uk (GBP 1,035 per adult, 2026).
uncertainty: There is no actual route for this couple, so the figure is what a long-stay resident on, say, a family or work visa pays. Private-cover estimate is weak.

statutory_must_pay.what: Immigration Health Surcharge, GBP 1,035 a year per adult, 2 x 1,035 / 12 = 172.50 a month, as in the first round.
